episodes.168210: Very hot temperatures developed on the afternoon of the 17th which generated scattered high based virga showers and a few thunderstorms. These virga showers and thunderstorms quickly became outflow dominant producing several severe wind gusts across the South Plains and Rolling Plains. One of these high-based showers collapsed near Slaton (Lubbock County) where extensive damage occurred. The Slaton Fire Department reported several five-inch tree limbs snapped in addition to several structures sustaining roof damage.||High wind reports from the Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet are listed below:||79 mph at Slaton (Lubbock County),|77 mph at Sundown (Cochran County),|76 mph at McAdoo (Dickens County),|69 mph at Abernathy (Hale County),|65 mph at Roaring Springs (Motley County), and|58 mph at Ralls (Crosby County).
episodes.168444: Multiple strong storms moved into the Nebraska Panhandle during the afternoon and early evening on the 17th. This included one severe storm that tracked from north of Scottsbluff southeast towards the I-80 corridor producing up to ping-pong ball sized hail. Numerous locations also received large accumulations of hail.
episodes.168483: A potent mid level shortwave combined with weak instability and strong shear to generate strong to severe storms across central and north-central Wisconsin during the evening hours on Wednesday (5/18).  The strongest storms produced wind damage and half dollar size hail.
episodes.168671: Several waterspouts were observed in association with a cumulus congestus cloud line from the Gulf side of the lower Florida Keys through waters west of Key West.
episodes.168680: Isolated thunderstorms developed in the southeastern Nebraska Panhandle during the early evening hours of May 17th. This activity tracked from Deuel and southern Garden county into Keith county before dissipating. Hail up to half dollar size and thunderstorm wind gusts to around 70 MPH were reported.
episodes.168847: An isolated supercell thunderstorm developed over Bottineau County, producing a tornado and reported one-inch diameter hail. The tornado touched down in an open field southeast of Landa. The tornado impacted no structures and so there was no damage to evaluate, thus rated EF-Unknown.
episodes.169257: First round of storms produced hail reports in northeast Nebraska in the early morning hours. A second round of storms produced hail reports in eastern Nebraska late in the evening.
episodes.169258: Storms produced several severe hail reports across southwest Iowa.
episodes.169418: A line of severe storms raced southeast across central and south central Kansas during the late evening and overnight hours of May 17th into early on May 18th, 2022. Wind speeds of 60 to 75 mph were common with these storms.  Tree limbs and power lines were blown down as well as several locations noting shingle loss.
episodes.169429: Cold front leads to strong to severe thunderstorms for portions of south central Nebraska during the evening of May 17th. The first thunderstorms of this event developed over southwest Furnas County between 4PM and 5PM CDT. The initial concern was the potential for landspouts, and at least two were reported in the area of Wilsonville and Beaver City. As is often the case with landspouts, these were very brief touchdowns, and no damage indicators could be found, so they were given an EFU, or unknown, rating. This initial setup for landspouts was fairly typical for this region in which steep low level lapse rates coincided with weak deep layer wind shear, weak low level convergence, and a weak surface front that provides abundant ambient surface vorticity. Eventually, between 5PM and 7PM, thunderstorms ���unzipped���, or developed further northeast in Kearney County, along the advancing cold front, which lead to upscale growth into a couple intense thunderstorm clusters. Large hail was the primary hazard with this activity, and for the most part ranged from quarter to golf ball size. However, up to 3 inch in diameter hail was reported in Harlan County. The thunderstorm clusters moved east and southeast, and eventually weakened and/or shifted in northern Kansas around 8PM CDT.||Another separate broken line of thunderstorms developed further north, from around Kearney to Columbus, between 9PM and 10PM. This activity persisted for a couple of hours before weakening. Once again, large hail was the primary threat, with penny to half dollar size hail reported in portions of Hall and Hamilton Counties.
episodes.169430: Cold front leads to strong to severe thunderstorms for portions of north central Kansas during the evening of May 17th. The first thunderstorms of this event developed over Norton County between 4PM and 5PM CDT. The initial concern was the potential for landspouts, and at least a few were reported just west of the local forecast area. Eventually, between 5PM and 7PM, thunderstorms grew upscale into a broken line as they moved into Phillips County at sub-severe levels. The line developed some organization and small bowing segment between 7:30PM and 8PM as it moved into Osborne County. Severe wind gusts near 60 MPH were measured at a mesonet site near Osborne, and estimated gusts up to 75 MPH were also reported in this area. The apex of the bowing segment exited the Hastings forecast area into central Kansas around 9PM to 10PM. The northern portion of the thunderstorm line extended into Mitchell County, but no severe gusts were measured or reported.
episodes.169587: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed into far northeastern Oklahoma from Kansas during the early morning hours of the 18th. The strongest storms produced damaging wind.
episodes.169623: A mesoscale convective complex moved southeastward across the region during the morning of the 18th. The complex weakened during the late morning with the loss of the low level jet and left an outflow boundary that focused storm development later that afternoon near the Arkansas border. Hail to golf balls in size and damaging winds were produced by the strongest storms.
episodes.169673: Scattered thunderstorms moved into western Oklahoma during the evening of the 17th producing isolated severe wind gusts. As storms decayed several heat bursts were also observed.
episodes.169727: Two large clusters of storms formed into a large QLCS and produced hail, damaging wind to as high as 85 mph, and flash flooding during the evening of 5/17.
episodes.169794: Strong to severe thunderstorms formed ahead of a mid-level shortwave and surface disturbance which moved through the Ohio Valley during the afternoon and evening hours on May 18th. Storms initially formed as part of an MCS which moved across southern Indiana and into central Kentucky. After the initial MCS dissipated, scattered cells formed along the southern flank of the antecedent MCS, causing wind damage and hail across central Kentucky.
episodes.170019: An area of low pressure moved across the Northland during the afternoon of the 18th. Storms developed ahead of an associated cold front and turned into a line of storms that worked across much of northeastern Minnesota and into northwest Wisconsin. The storms were mainly wind producers with numerous reports of trees down and minor structure damage as the moved through. Some hail was reported as well, but was mainly around an inch or less. An embedded EF-0 tornado was confirmed just north of the Duluth area and produced mainly tree damage.
episodes.170021: An area of low pressure moved across the Northland during the afternoon of the 18th. Storms developed ahead of an associated cold front and turned into a line of storms that worked across much of northeastern Minnesota and into northwest Wisconsin. The storms were mainly wind producers with numerous reports of trees down and minor structure damage as the moved through. Some hail was reported as well with the largest stones being golf ball sized.
episodes.170022: An area of low pressure moved across the Northland during the afternoon of the 18th. Storms developed ahead of an associated cold front and turned into a line of storms that worked across much of northeastern Minnesota and into northwest Wisconsin and western Lake Superior. Winds were generally sub severe over the lake, but a few gusts 43 and 40 mph were recorded as they moved along the South Shore.
episodes.170070: A weak cold front moved south across extreme Southwest Nebraska and Northwest Kansas during the afternoon hours on the 17th. As storms developed along the front, brief landspout tornadoes were reported in northern Decatur and Gove counties. These stayed mainly over fields, producing no damage. There were also reports of pea to quarter sized hail with the line of storms. The largest hail report was also located in Decatur County in the town of Jennings. During the evening, a line of storms moved east across the Colorado border eventually connecting with the earlier line of storms impacting areas along I-70 as far east as Beloit, Kansas. When the storms moved over Sherman County it produced up to 58 mph wind gusts.
episodes.170166: During the evening hours, a line of showers and storms developed over Eastern Colorado. As the line move over Yuma and Kit Carson counties, 60 mph wind gusts occurred with some small tree limb damage reported near Idalia, Colorado.
episodes.170210: An organized complex of thunderstorms moved through east central Kansas during the late evening of May 17. A couple strong wind gusts and some minor damage occurred with these storms.
episodes.170214: In the afternoon of May 17 a complex of severe thunderstorms moved through northern Missouri, bringing some minor wind damage and marginally severe hail. Later in the evening another convective complex moved into the the southern KC metro, causing some strong winds after sunset.
episodes.170327: A low level jet of over 30 kts coupled with ample low level moisture with dewpoints into the 50s to near 60 helped to aid for MLCAPE values over 2000 J/kg. As a result, 1-2 inch hail reports occurred mostly in the isolated cells but a couple wind gust reports later in the evening when storms became more clustered before becoming linear further northeast.
episodes.170471: Isolated severe thunderstorms moved across portions of eastern North Dakota and west-central Minnesota. Severe reports primarily consisted of damaging wind gusts, with only small hail reported.

A brief tornado tracked approximately west to east from north of the intersection of Lismore Road and Arnold Road, across Eagle Lake Road, and then across Jean Duluth Road before ending near Lady Nicole Lane east of Jean Duluth Road. This tornado caused numerous tree damage along its path, with a consistent tree fall pattern indicative of a tornado, but was unlikely above EF-0 in strength. While a few trees were snapped near the base, the vast majority of tree damage was large branches and trees that have bent over, with a few uprooted trees. The estimated maximum wind speed of this tornado was 85 mph. There was no known property damage outside of the tree damage.
